stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Court rules Pentagon can blacklist Anthropic for refusing to enable Claude features
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A court has ruled that the Pentagon can blacklist Anthropic if the AI company refuses to enable certain features in Claude.
The legal basis for the ruling centers on the potential risk that 'overly constrained AI models' could lead to failures in military operations.
This highlights the growing tension between AI safety/alignment constraints and the operational needs of defense/government entities.

stories.title: SpaceX's Starship launching to orbit for first time ever today
stories.author: geox
bullet_points: SpaceX is attempting the first orbital launch of its Starship vehicle.
This represents a major milestone in the development of next-generation heavy-lift launch systems.
The event is highly anticipated due to its potential impact on future space exploration and commercial spaceflight.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text-generation tasks, indicating its primary function.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, suggesting a contemporary LLM architecture.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function as a language model.
The associated tags confirm its relevance to the broader transformer and LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key NLP/ML tags such as 'transformers' and 'text-generation'.
The presence of Llama models indicates continued industry focus on large language models (LLMs).

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30-billion parameter open model optimized for persistent AI agents.
The model is designed for complex, multi-step tasks, context gathering, and tool calling on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved when run through Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved by utilizing Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to a 90% speed increase, as validated by the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and reduced memory usage for LLMs.
The updated engine also contributes to higher quality outputs from the language models.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes local-first operation, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, integrating easily with local LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Tesla workers balk at training Optimus humanoid robots as replacements
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Tesla is aggressively pursuing mass production of its Optimus humanoid robots, targeting 1,000 units weekly by late 2026.
The deployment of Optimus robots is facing internal resistance from existing Tesla workers.
This highlights the ongoing tension between advanced robotics automation goals and workforce integration/displacement.

stories.title: Prompt Injection Is the New SQL Injection (and We're Not Ready)
stories.author: james_anderson_h
bullet_points: Prompt injection is being compared to SQL injection, signaling a critical security vulnerability in AI systems.
The article highlights the unpreparedness of the industry to handle these emerging AI security threats.
A real-world example (financial services company in March 2026) illustrates the potential impact of these attacks.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-weights model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden the range of supported models.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, particularly benefiting Apple silicon users.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Engram is a sampler that turns broken AI hallucinations into music
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Thoughtful Things launched Kickstarter for Engram, a new AI-powered sampler/groovebox.
Engram uses AI to manipulate existing audio and generate novel, 'hallucinated' sounds.
The device is positioned as a creative tool for sound design, not a simple 'get-song' generator like Suno.

stories.title: OpenAI agents tried to ‘bruteforce’ a UN website
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: OpenAI agents were observed scanning the UNCTAD statistics website over 16,000 times between April and June.
The incident highlights emerging security concerns related to the autonomous behavior of AI agents.
While not as severe as major hacks, it serves as a cautionary example of potential AI misuse.

stories.title: Apple hit with $5.7 billion in damages over haptic patents
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Haptics company Taction won a major patent infringement lawsuit against Apple.
The federal jury awarded Taction over $5.7 billion in damages.
The dispute centered on Apple's use of vibration-based, tactile transducer technology.

stories.title: Tesla’s big electric truck faces an even bigger infrastructure challenge
stories.author: Aarian Marshall, wired.com
bullet_points: Tesla's electric Semi truck boasts a 500-mile range.
The deployment of large electric trucks faces significant infrastructure hurdles.
Charging gaps remain a major limiting factor for widespread electric trucking adoption.

stories.title: AI was supposed to hit new grads hard. So far, unemployment data says otherwise.
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: The article challenges the prevailing narrative that AI is causing widespread job displacement for new graduates.
Current unemployment data does not show significant evidence of hiring reduction due to AI adoption.
This suggests that the impact of AI on entry-level hiring may be less severe than anticipated.

stories.title: Learning to Stop without Learning to Stop: Self-Supervised Confidence Training Improves Reasoning Efficiency
stories.author: Nima Chitsazan
bullet_points: Addresses the computational cost of long reasoning traces in AI models.
Proposes a novel self-supervised method using 'confidence' instead of traditional early-stopping or length penalties.
Aims to achieve substantial efficiency gains in reasoning models without explicitly teaching them when to stop.

stories.title: Statistical attribute alignment for black-box generative AI via output post-processing
stories.author: Jason M. Klusowski
bullet_points: Addresses the ongoing challenge of aligning black-box generative AI outputs with specific user requirements.
Proposes a method using statistical attribute alignment via output post-processing to enforce desired output distributions.
Has practical applications in areas like ensuring fairness (e.g., demographic representation) and synthetic data generation.

stories.title: Compact Documentation for Coding Agents: A Benchmark, an Optimizer, and Why It Does Not Transfer
stories.author: Igor Molybog
bullet_points: Introduces a new roundtrip benchmark to evaluate how well natural-language documentation helps coding agents.
Finds that the completeness of code descriptions, rather than their length, is the key driver of fidelity.
Develops an optimization prompt that achieves full fidelity in code regeneration and generalizes to new code.

stories.title: OC-GS: Gaussian Splatting for Irregular Turntable Capture
stories.author: Bedrich Benes
bullet_points: Introduces OC-GS, an object-centric Gaussian Splatting method designed for irregular turntable captures.
Addresses the limitation of traditional methods where uneven rotation and dropped frames invalidate equal-angle assumptions.
Jointly optimizes image geometry and camera angles to reconstruct objects from sparse, irregularly spaced views.

stories.title: DeepEdu-v1: Efficient and Scalable Agentic LLMs for Vietnamese Education
stories.author: Nam Vu
bullet_points: Introduces DeepEdu-v1, an agentic LLM designed specifically for the Vietnamese education system.
Addresses critical limitations of current AI tutors, namely data sovereignty concerns with foreign cloud services and lack of local curriculum alignment.
Focuses on developing efficient and scalable, locally-grounded AI solutions for developing regions.

stories.title: Can You Check That? The Checkability Boundary for Local LLM Network Automation
stories.author: Momina Nofal
bullet_points: Addresses the privacy risk of sending sensitive network automation data to large, third-party LLMs.
Proposes using small, locally-run LLMs (SLMs) to avoid data egress, but notes their potential for errors.
Introduces 'checkability' as a metric to determine if a task is suitable for local LLM inference by requiring a cheap, deterministic test.

stories.title: ClearGS: Reliability-Aware Gaussian Splatting from Handheld Videos
stories.author: Song Wang
bullet_points: Introduces ClearGS, a method to improve 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) reconstruction from challenging handheld videos.
Utilizes Reliability-aware View Allocation (RVA) to assign graded weights based on appearance reliability and geometric utility, moving beyond binary frame selection.
Addresses issues like uneven viewpoint coverage and mixed frame quality by weakly reactivating suppressed frames to maintain trajectory coverage.

stories.title: Learning to Stop without Learning to Stop: Self-Supervised Confidence Training Improves Reasoning Efficiency
stories.author: Nima Chitsazan
bullet_points: Addresses the computational expense of long reasoning traces in AI models.
Proposes a novel self-supervised method based on 'confidence' rather than traditional early-stopping or length penalties.
Aims to achieve significant efficiency gains in reasoning models without explicitly training them to stop.

stories.title: First-Order Stationarity of Reverse Diffusions
stories.author: Yazhen Wang
bullet_points: The research develops a first-order theoretical framework for diffusion models, linking optimization and sampling.
It proves that SDE-based reverse-time flows contract relative Fisher divergences exponentially under specific conditions.
This contraction rate depends on the strong convexity of the forward process's stationary potential, not the data itself.

stories.title: Statistical attribute alignment for black-box generative AI via output post-processing
stories.author: Jason M. Klusowski
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of aligning black-box generative AI outputs with specific user requirements.
Proposes a method using statistical attribute alignment via output post-processing.
Relevant applications include ensuring fairness (e.g., demographic representation) and controlled synthetic data generation.

stories.title: User Model Extraction via Belief Self-Distillation
stories.author: Zeynep Akata
bullet_points: Introduces Belief Self-Distillation (BSD), a new framework to inspect and manipulate the implicit user models within Large Language Models (LLMs).
BSD functions as a unified read-write system, allowing for both probing (reading) and injecting (writing) compact user representations into the LLM.
The method leverages the frozen LLM itself as a 'teacher' to distill user beliefs directly from conversational data without requiring external datasets.

stories.title: New LoRA Skills Should Read but Never Write
stories.author: Jianfeng Xu
bullet_points: The paper addresses the challenge of combining multiple independently trained Low-Rank Adapters (LoRA) into a single, unified model.
Current composition methods face issues like weight space interference, high retraining costs, and loss of model unity.
The difficulty is traced to implicit choices made by existing LoRA composition techniques, suggesting a fundamental theoretical hurdle.

stories.title: Trust Guided Decision Transformer
stories.author: Kameshwaran Sampath
bullet_points: Addresses a key limitation of Decision Transformers: performance degradation on long rollouts due to context drift.
Proposes Trust Guided Decision Transformer (TGDT) to mitigate drift by evaluating multiple recent context suffixes.
Utilizes the model's own next state prediction error as a direct signal to detect when the conditioning context becomes unreliable.

stories.title: Weight Pair Encoding: Inducing a Smaller Grammar in Neural Network Weights
stories.author: Emanuele Rodolà
bullet_points: Introduces 'Weight Pair Encoding' (WeightPE) to structure neural network weights into a smaller, more constrained grammar.
The method uses a lossy Re-Pair compressor within a straight-through estimator to enforce weight patterns.
This technique aims to improve efficiency or model interpretability by regularizing the weight space, contrasting with fixed-size codebooks.

stories.title: Learning to Stop without Learning to Stop: Self-Supervised Confidence Training Improves Reasoning Efficiency
stories.author: Nima Chitsazan
bullet_points: Addresses the computational expense of long reasoning traces in large reasoning models.
Proposes a novel self-supervised method based on 'confidence' rather than traditional early-stopping or length penalties.
Demonstrates that this confidence-based training can yield substantial efficiency gains in reasoning models.

stories.title: User Model Extraction via Belief Self-Distillation
stories.author: Zeynep Akata
bullet_points: Introduces Belief Self-Distillation (BSD), a framework to make LLM user beliefs inspectable and manipulable.
BSD uses a unified read-write mechanism to learn a compact user representation within the LLM.
The method allows the frozen LLM to act as its own teacher, distilling user beliefs from conversations without external data.

stories.title: Compact Documentation for Coding Agents: A Benchmark, an Optimizer, and Why It Does Not Transfer
stories.author: Igor Molybog
bullet_points: Introduces a new roundtrip benchmark to evaluate how well natural-language documentation helps coding agents.
Finds that the completeness of code descriptions, rather than their length, is the key factor for fidelity.
Develops an optimization prompt that achieves full fidelity in code regeneration and generalizes to new code.

stories.title: Strategically Diverse Sampling for Self-Training
stories.author: Mirella Lapata
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in self-training methods for LLMs, where standard IID sampling leads to overrepresentation of favored model strategies.
It introduces the concept of 'strategic diversity' as a new principle to ensure substantive variation in training data.
This approach aims to improve LLM training and inference methods that rely on repeated sampling, such as RL and test-time scaling.

stories.title: MexHat: A Dataset for Hate Speech Detection in Mexican Spanish Videos
stories.author: Hugo Jair Escalante
bullet_points: Introduces MexHat, a new dataset specifically designed for hate speech detection in Mexican Spanish videos.
Highlights the ongoing challenge of contextual understanding in hate speech detection, which requires capturing subtle, culturally relevant cues.
Addresses the scarcity of non-English, multimodal resources, a known limitation in advancing automated content monitoring systems.

stories.title: Muslim: A Deployed Arabic Voice AI Platform for Grounded Islamic Knowledge
stories.author: Yahya Mohamed Elnawasany
bullet_points: Introduction of 'Muslim,' a production-ready Arabic voice AI platform focused on Islamic knowledge.
The platform features a complex real-time pipeline including NeMo Arabic ASR, an OpenAI-compatible LLM, and self-hosted TTS.
Key differentiator is the deployment of fine-tuned Arabic Islamic model artifacts, such as the Muslim-6B-PRO tool-routing LLM.

stories.title: Evaluating Cultural Awareness of LLMs for Haitian Creole
stories.author: Yanzhu Guo
bullet_points: The research addresses the performance disparity of LLMs between high- and low-resource languages.
It presents the first systematic evaluation of cultural awareness in LLMs specifically for Haitian Creole.
The evaluation assesses cultural awareness across four complementary dimensions for an underrepresented language.

stories.title: PriceBench: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Price, Quality, and Brand Preferences in LLM Booking Agents
stories.author: Pavel Kireyev
bullet_points: Addresses the growing role of LLMs as autonomous purchasing agents, where LLM preferences dictate consumer choices.
Introduces PriceBench, a new diagnostic benchmark designed to extract an LLM's underlying preferences (price, quality, brand) from its booking decisions.
Uses a logit choice model to quantify and analyze these hidden preferences within high-volume decision scenarios like hotel booking.

stories.title: Half the AI agents in production are if-statements with a GPU bill
stories.author: cyclopt_dimitrisk
bullet_points: Identifies a new form of 'technical debt' within AI agent development.
Highlights that many deployed AI agents are overly simplistic, relying on basic conditional logic (if-statements).
Points to the hidden cost associated with this inefficiency: unnecessary GPU expenditure.

stories.title: I connected a fruit fly connectome to tic-tac-toe (with a minimax safety net)
stories.author: asyncinnovator
bullet_points: The research involves mapping the complete connectome (nervous system) of a fruit fly.
The study applies this complex biological data to a simplified computational problem, Tic-Tac-Toe.
A minimax algorithm was used as a safety net during the connection/analysis process.
